context: Zoomable circle packing of ~300 synthetic Wikipedia articles in 6 top-level categories and subcategories, with circle area encoding article word count
first_impression: Structurally honest encoding — d3.pack() correctly uses area-based sizing (radius = sqrt(value/π)) so circle area faithfully represents word count without lie factor.
what_works: d3.pack() inherently implements area-correct scaling (not radius-linear), so doubling word count correctly doubles area; categorical color encoding uses a qualitatively distinct 6-color palette (Tol Bright) via scaleOrdinal, which is appropriate for nominal categories.
what_doesnt: The underlying word-count distribution is explicitly skewed (pow(rand, 0.5) * 48000 — a right-skewed power distribution) but this skewness is never communicated to the viewer, so users may misread relative sizes of large vs. small articles; no key functions in data joins, which is acceptable for this static render but would cause visual corruption on any live data update.
